title: Studies of NGC 6720 with Calibrated HST/WFC3 Emission-line Filter Images. I. Structure and Evolution

evidence.locator: Sect. III.1, restating O'Dell, Sabbadin & Henney (2007): from flux-calibrated long-slit spectra, with all motion radial and in proportion to distance, expansion is 0.65 km/s per arcsec from the star; the Main Ring's semi-major axis is 44 arcsec along position angle about 60 degrees and its semi-minor axis 30 arcsec; the pole is tipped 6.5 +/- 2 degrees from the line of sight, the south-west end of the Main Ring moving away; the gas is concentrated toward the equatorial plane. Sect. III.3: velocity ellipses fitted to the spectra give the Main Ring 19 +/- 2 km/s along the line of sight in [N II] and [S II] and 9 +/- 2 km/s in [O III], and the central region, assigned to the polar Lobes, 37 km/s in [S II], 36 in [N II], 28 in [O III], 27 in H-alpha and 20 in He II (34 km/s adopted); the dark knots show best against background material; the paper has no evidence about the form of the Lobes. Sect. III.4: the Inner Halo's loops lie almost all within 65 arcsec of the star; the Outer Halo is a thin shell of radius 115 arcsec.
